O.outcome_detail: Adequacy of classroom space for projected 2025–26 enrollment

result.effect: 82% sufficient; 249 LEAs (18%) insufficient; 946 additional classrooms needed

cells.quote: Eighty-two percent of LEAs reported that they had sufficient classroom space for anticipated enrollment in the 2025–26 school year. However, the 249 LEAs (18% of all respondents) that indicated not having enough classroom space reported needing a total of 946 additional UPk classrooms to accommodate projected enrollment by 2025–26.
cells.note: The study text reports descriptive proportions and need estimates, not a comparative effect between treatment and comparison conditions. The medium-sized versus small/large LEA percentages appear only in the wiki entry, so they were not used.

D.comparison: stand-alone CSPP, Head Start, or other early learning classroom

O.outcome_detail: share of UPK classrooms by classroom model

cells.quote: In the 2022–23 school year, almost half (46%) of the state’s 15,425 UPk classrooms were Tk stand-alone classrooms. One third (33%) of UPk classrooms operated in LEAs were stand-alone classes for non-Tk programs such as CSPP, Head Start, or other early learning programs.
cells.note: Descriptive survey prevalence, not an instructional-effect comparison.

O.outcome_detail: share of UPK classrooms by classroom model

cells.quote: In the 2022–23 school year, almost half (46%) of the state’s 15,425 UPk classrooms were Tk stand-alone classrooms. Eighteen percent were Tk–kindergarten combination classes, and the rest (2%) were combination classes of Tk and either CSPP or locally funded preschool.
cells.note: Descriptive survey prevalence, not an instructional-effect comparison.

O.outcome_detail: share and prominence of reported UPK implementation challenges

result.effect: more than one third of LEAs; facilities identified as a top challenge

cells.quote: Most LEAs had sufficient classroom space for projected TK enrollment, although facilities remain a top challenge in UPK implementation. ... Furthermore, in an open-ended question on UPK challenges, more than one third of LEAs noted facilities-related challenges such as finding funding to update existing facilities to meet requirements, having age-appropriate bathrooms and playgrounds, and improving spaces for early learners.
cells.note: The comparison with other challenge categories is implied by the report's characterization of facilities as a top challenge.

D.treatment: LEAs planning to offer early-admittance TK
D.comparison: LEAs not planning to offer it or unsure

O.outcome_detail: Planned transitional-kindergarten eligibility expansion

result.effect: 39% planned to offer ETK; 34% did not; 27% were unsure

cells.quote:
More than a third of LEAs (39%) reported plans to offer ETK.
• About one third (34%) did not plan to offer ETK, although a small percentage plan to begin offering ETK in 2023–24 (2%) or 2024–25 (1%).
• About one quarter (27%) were unsure of their plans to offer ETK.
cells.note: This is a descriptive comparison of survey-reported plans, not a manipulated treatment effect. The study states that intended plans may differ from actual implementation.

D.treatment: LEAs planning only full-day TK or both full- and part-day TK

O.outcome_detail: Planned length of the TK instructional day

result.effect: 79% planned some full-day TK; 21% planned only part-day TK

cells.quote: Nearly 4 in 5 LEAs plan to offer full-day TK at some or all sites: 68% plan to offer only full-day TK, while 11% plan to offer both full- and part-day classes. The remainder (21%) plan to offer only part-day TK classes.
cells.note: The report describes the distribution of intended program models; it does not establish that full-day TK produces better outcomes.

O.outcome_detail: Facility-space adequacy for projected TK enrollment

cells.quote: The majority of LEAs (73%) indicated that they have sufficient facility space to meet projected TK enrollment, although facilities are a top concern for others.
cells.note: This is a descriptive survey contrast between LEAs’ reported facility conditions.

result.effect: Approximately four fifths of LEAs reported not having enough qualified staff

cells.note: The study reports LEAs’ intended workforce conditions, not an intervention effect or a measured learning outcome.
